bug_description.original: A crash occurs when parsing 1 byte truncated omf files.
bug_description.normalized: When radare2's `ia_fuzz` harness writes the staged one-byte file into a malloc-backed IO buffer and issues `oba 0`, bin-plugin autodetection reaches the OMF plugin's `check_buffer`. `check_buffer` reads byte 0 and accepts `0x82` as a plausible OMF record tag. It then materializes the whole input with `r_buf_data()` and gets a heap buffer whose length is still only 1 byte, but immediately interprets `buf + 1` as the 16-bit `rec_size` field before any lower-bound check proves that the 4-byte OMF header exists. AddressSanitizer reports the first out-of-bounds read at `libr/bin/p/bin_omf.c:37` because the one-byte allocation returned by `r_buf_data()` has no valid byte at offset 1. The adjacent `str_size` read from `buf + 3` is likewise unguarded in the vulnerable source, and the patch replaces both raw pointer dereferences with bounded `r_buf_read_*` helpers plus an explicit `r_buf_size()` query.

source.description: First project-code read on the vulnerable path. `check_buffer` reads the first byte of the attacker-controlled buffer into `ch`, creating the record-tag state that decides whether the OMF parser continues.
source.value_from: The staged PoC at `gt_results/arvo_15003/poc` has sha256 `a5ab782c805e8bfbe34cb65742a0471cf5a53a97f0a1160ab6cccbb64c9131ce` and consists of exactly one byte `0x82`. This call copies that sole byte into `ch`.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

root_cause.description: `check_buffer` dereferences the OMF header's two-byte size field from `buf + 1` without first rejecting buffers shorter than the 4-byte header. The later size predicate is below this dereference, so it cannot protect truncated inputs. The patch fixes this exact obligation by switching to bounded `r_buf_read_le16_at()` / `r_buf_read_at()` helpers and querying the buffer size explicitly.

sink.description: ASan sink. `ut8p_bw(buf + 1)` performs the first out-of-bounds read from the 1-byte heap buffer returned by `r_buf_data()`, producing the observed heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1 at `libr/bin/p/bin_omf.c:37`.
sink.note: The macro `ut8p_bw(x)` expands to `((x)[0] | ((x)[1] << 8))`, so with `x = buf + 1` the first load already touches `buf[1]`, which is one byte past the end of the region `[buf, buf + 1)` allocated in `get_whole_buf`.

tainted_value_origin.description: This is the first point where the attacker-controlled buffer is materialized as a contiguous byte array and exact length pair. For the staged witness, `buf` points to the 1-byte heap copy allocated by `get_whole_buf` and `length` becomes 1, which is the extent later violated by `ut8p_bw(buf + 1)`.

parser_admitted.description: The PoC byte is `0x82`, so this rejection test is false and `check_buffer` continues into OMF-specific header parsing instead of returning early.

fine_trace.note: Reads the first attacker-controlled byte from `b` into `ch`. For the staged witness, the call succeeds and stores `0x82`, because the file is exactly one byte long and that byte is `0x82`.
The non-OMF rejection is not taken because `ch == 0x82`. This control decision keeps execution on the OMF parser path and makes the later header reads reachable for the one-byte witness.

Materializes the entire input as a contiguous heap buffer and records its size. For this PoC, `length` becomes 1 and ASan's allocation stack shows `get_whole_buf` allocated the 1-byte region `[buf, buf + 1)` before returning it through `r_buf_data()`.

Root cause. This statement treats bytes starting at `buf + 1` as the fixed two-byte OMF record-size field even though step 3 established that the materialized buffer length is only 1. There is no earlier lower-bound or bounded-read guard in `check_buffer`; the later predicate `if (str_size + 2 != rec_size || length < rec_size + 3)` is sequenced after this statement and cannot protect truncated inputs.

ASan sink. Step 4 reaches `ut8p_bw(buf + 1)`, and that macro expands to `((x)[0] | ((x)[1] << 8))`; with `x = buf + 1`, the first subread touches `buf[1]`. Because step 3's heap buffer has valid data only at `buf[0]`, this load immediately reads one byte past the 1-byte allocation and AddressSanitizer reports `heap-buffer-overflow` READ of size 1 at line 37.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: n/a: ASan's allocation context is the 1-byte whole-buffer copy allocated in `get_whole_buf`; the root cause is the later missing lower-bound check in `check_buffer` before reading `buf + 1`.

poc.trigger: Run the staged PoC through `ia_fuzz`. The file is exactly one byte `0x82`; line 13's `oba 0` command reaches `check_buffer`, which accepts that tag and overruns the 1-byte heap buffer while parsing `rec_size` from `buf + 1` before `ia` executes.
